character_facts: Aghnar is carrying or protecting Oda while badly wounded himself.
Aghnar is analytical under pressure, arguing that no enemy is truly invincible.
Aghnar is determined to continue despite despair and physical danger.
Oda is alive but unconscious or incapacitated, with severe mental or neurological harm described in dialogue.
Tonto is a small robot who speaks at length and appears medically relevant to Oda's survival.
The cetacyborgs are active antagonists physically blocking Aghnar's path.
characters_present: An unidentified surviving witch mentioned in dialogue but not clearly shown
continuity_links: This page follows a battle that left Oda gravely injured.
It sets up an immediate attempt to reach the Metabunker for treatment.
It foreshadows the next chapter or episode, "The Possession of Oda," as the continuation of this crisis.
dialogue_meaning: The injured woman has a beating heart, but her mind or brain has been catastrophically affected by the battle.
The male lead believes immediate surgery in the Metabunker by Tonto could save her.
The cetacyborg enemies present themselves as an inescapable blockade.
The man rejects the idea that the monsters are unbeatable and insists they must have some vulnerability.
He is emotionally strained but remains determined to continue.
Tonto shifts from comic interruption to strategic information, saying the key knowledge about the cetacyborgs' weakness may be lost with the last surviving witch.
The dialogue also states that Aghnar will get past the cetacyborgs and that Oda will recover, framing that outcome as expected by the speaker.
locations: A combat-damaged interior passage or chamber
The Metabunker, mentioned as the intended destination
lore_facts: The Metabunker is a place with medical or surgical capability.
Tonto is capable of performing or assisting in an operation.
Cetacyborgs are creatures created by the witches of Shabda-Oud.
Within this page's dialogue, the cetacyborgs are said to have a weak spot.
Only one of the witches is said to remain alive at this moment.
Knowledge of the cetacyborgs' weakness is tied to that surviving witch.
The next episode is titled "The Possession of Oda."
plot_events: The man confirms the woman is still alive physically but mentally devastated by battle.
He decides to rush her to the Metabunker so Tonto may be able to operate on her.
Hostile cetacyborgs block the route and taunt him, saying escape is impossible.
The man reasons that the attackers must have a weak point because their creators would not make truly invincible monsters.
Despite the situation, he resolves to attempt the impossible and push forward.
A small robot named Tonto interrupts and begins giving information.
Tonto states that only one witch is still alive and that the secret of the cetacyborgs' weakness may die with her.
The page ends with a next-episode teaser: "The Possession of Oda."
uncertainties: Some dialogue is small and stylized, so exact wording is hard to read; summary is based on legible portions.
The page source says p27, but the printed page number visible in the image is 28.
One speech balloon contains a convoluted line about ancestry and the current Metabaron; its precise wording is difficult to parse from the image alone.
The surviving witch is mentioned in dialogue, but her identity is not established on this page.
visual_summary: A wounded dark-haired man in armor carries or kneels over an unconscious woman whose body shows heavy injury. He moves through a corridor crowded by hostile, insectlike or cyborg figures while speaking urgently about saving her and overcoming seemingly invincible enemies. Large close-ups emphasize his desperation. In the lower section, a small round robot addresses him and explains that only one witch remains alive and that the secret weakness of the attacking cetacyborgs may die with her. A caption at the bottom announces the next episode, "The Possession of Oda."
